heading: Rightmost = Last Node Per Level
body:
Use **level-order BFS** to visit nodes level by level. Track how many nodes are in each level — the **last node** you process is the rightmost.

- Count nodes before processing a level
- When `i == level_size - 1`, you're at the rightmost node

heading: Why Queue, Not Stack?
body:
BFS needs a **queue** (FIFO) to process nodes left-to-right, level-by-level.

- Add children to the queue as you go
- The last node dequeued at each level is the rightmost

label: Crux · Python

q: What is the time complexity of this solution?
explain: We visit each node exactly once during BFS traversal.
